title: The dropped oxygen tank that crippled Apollo 13
hook: A dropped oxygen tank nearly stranded three astronauts near the Moon.
summary: A tank dropped in 1968 and heater switches rated for the wrong voltage set up the Apollo 13 explosion, yet the crew survived using the lunar module as a lifeboat.
sources: NASA Apollo 13 Review Board report (Cortright Report), 1970: tank dropped about two inches in 1965 handling, thermostats rated 28 V exposed to 65 V ground power, insulation damaged.
Encyclopaedia Britannica and Wikipedia, Apollo 13: explosion on April 13, 1970, crew used lunar module as lifeboat, splashdown April 17.

lines.text: A dropped oxygen tank nearly stranded three astronauts near the Moon.
Years earlier, workers let it fall about two inches.
Later, its heater was tested on sixty-five volts, but its switches were built for twenty-eight.
They welded shut, and the wire insulation inside burned away.
On Apollo Thirteen, a spark in that tank blew off a panel.
Air and power ran low, so the crew used their landing craft as a lifeboat.
One unchecked switch almost ended the mission.

post.caption:
A tiny switch rated for the wrong voltage set up one of space's biggest rescues.
Would you have trusted the lifeboat?
Follow @unt.oldfiles for a new untold story every day.
